name: Elkanah
overview: Elkanah is a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically identified as a Kohathite. He is noted for being the father of Zophai and the son of Mahath, situating him within a Levitical lineage important for priestly duties. His role is grounded in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Levi.
namesAndTitles: The name Elkanah means 'G-d [El] has possessed,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew proper name. This name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:26 and is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Elkanah as the father of Zophai and Tohu, as inferred from 1 Chronicles 6:26. Beyond these relationships and his descent from Mahath, no additional family details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Elkanah's significance lies in his place within the Levitical priestly genealogy, as a Kohathite, which underscores the continuity of priestly service in Israel. His lineage connects to the broader biblical narrative of God's appointed ministers, highlighting the faithfulness of God's covenant through generations. This genealogical record preserves the heritage of those serving in God's sanctuary.
